experiments.reasoning: Observation of antiseptic effects of plant substances on animal humours compared to water and salt.
experiments.description: Used decoctions and infusions (Wormwood, Bark, Chamomile, Snake-root) to preserve Yolks of Eggs compared to Water and Sea-Salt; later compared Salt of Hartshorn against Sea-Salt.
experiments.quote: I likewise found that Salt of Hartshorn preserved this Substance better than four times its Weight of Sea-Salt.
experiments.outcome: Salt of Hartshorn preserved the substance better than four times its weight of Sea-Salt.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of antiseptic effects of various chemicals on Ox's Gall.
experiments.description: Small quantities of Lye of Tartar, Spirit of Hartshorn, crude Sal Ammoniac, saline Mixture, and plant solutions mixed with Ox's Gall.
experiments.quote: Ox's Gall was kept some time from Putrefaction by small Quantities of Lye of Tartar, Spirit of Hartshorn, crude Sal Ammoniac, and the saline Mixture, and still longer by a Decoction of Wormwood, Infusions of Chamomile-flowers, and of Snake-root; by Solutions of Myrrh, Camphire, and Salt of Amber
experiments.outcome: Most substances preserved Gall better than Sea-Salt; Nitre failed.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Test of Nitre on Ox's Gall compared to its effect on Flesh.
experiments.description: Comparing Nitre against Crude Sal Ammoniac and Sea-Salt in keeping Flesh sweet and preserving Gall.
experiments.quote: Only Nitre failed; which, tho' four times stronger than Sea-Salt in keeping Flesh sweet, is inferior to it in preserving Gall
experiments.outcome: Nitre emitted Air (fermented) and allowed Gall to putrefy; Sal Ammoniac > Nitre > Sea Salt.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Test of antiseptic efficacy of plant infusions on Serum of Human Blood compared to Flesh.
experiments.description: Mixed Decoction of Bark, Infusion of Snake-root, Saffron, and Camphire with Serum of human Blood.
experiments.quote: The last Trial was with the Serum of human Blood, which was preferred by a Decotion of the Bark, and an Infusion of Snake-root, nor with lef Sfficacy than Flesh.
experiments.outcome: Bark and Snake-root preferred; Saffron and Camphire less effective than with Flesh.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Camomile's effect on Egg Yolk putrefaction.
experiments.description: Diluted Yolk with Water, added few drops of strong Infusion of Camomile-flowers, corked, and kept near a Fire.
experiments.quote: A Portion of this, being diluted with Water, flood till it corrupted; when a few Drops were put into a Phial with two Ounces of pure Water, and about twice as many Drops were mixed with a strong Infusion of Camomile-flowers.
experiments.outcome: Water caused putrid smell; Camomile mixture smelled of Flowers only.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of contagion via putrid thread spreading putrefaction.
experiments.description: Cut a Bit of putrid Egg Yolk (thread dipped), put into Phial with fresh Yolk + Water. Control Phial with fresh Yolk + Water.
experiments.quote: In the Yolk of an Egg, already putrid, a small Thread was dipped, and a small Bit of this was cut off and put into a Phial, with Half of the Yolk of a new-laid Egg diluted with Water.
experiments.outcome: Putrefaction perceived sooner in the contaminated Phial than the control.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Systematic observation of air conditions on meat putrefaction.
experiments.description: Observation of how putrid parts disperse with wind vs stagnate in confined air.
experiments.quote: In this manner the Putrefaction of Meat advances quicker in a confined than a free Air
experiments.outcome: Putrefaction advances quicker in confined air; stagnation excites it to Corruption.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Volatile Salts' effect on Fibres in warm infusion.
experiments.description: Tested Volatile Salts in warm Infusions compared to Water.
experiments.quote: yet, in warm Infusions, a small Quantity of these Salts will soften and resolve the Fibres, more than Water does by itself.
experiments.outcome: Volatile Salts soften/resolve Fibres in warm infusions, unlike in dry form.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Volatile Salts' ability to preserve dry meat.
experiments.description: Kept a small Piece of Flesh in a Phial preserved only with Salt of Hartthorn (Hartshorn) since the Beginning of June.
experiments.quote: For, so little do these Salts putrefy, or even resolve the Fibres, when applied dry, that I have kept, since the Beginning of june last, notwithstand-ing the excesive Heats, a small Piece of Flesh in a Phial, preserved only with Salt of Hartthorn, at present perfectly sound, and firmer than when first salted.
experiments.outcome: Flesh preserved perfectly sound and firmer than when first salted.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of vegetable plants (Carrots/Cabbage) on Putrefaction.
experiments.description: Tested Carrots, Turneps, Garlick, Onions, Celery, Cabbage, and Colewort.
experiments.quote: From the Specimens we had of the antiforbutic Plants, it is likewise probable none of that Tribe will prove septic. Horse-radish, one of the most acrid, is a very powerful Antiseptic. And tho' Carrots, Turneps, Garlick, Onions, Celery, Cabbage, and Colewort, were tried (as Alcarecents) they did not hasten, but somewhat retarded, the Putrefaction.
experiments.outcome: Carrots, Turneps, etc. did not hasten putrefaction, but somewhat retarded it.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of farinaeous vegetables (Grains) on Putrefaction.
experiments.description: Tested white Bread in Infusion, Decoctions of Flour, Barley, and Oatmeal.
experiments.quote: The Case was different with such farinaeous Vegetables as were examined; viz. white Bread in Infusion, Decoctions of Flour, Barley, and Oatmeal; for these did not at all retard Putrefaction; but, after it was somewhat advanced, they check'd it, by turning four.
experiments.outcome: Grains check'd putrefaction after advancing it via acidification (generated much Air).
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of animal substances (Cantharides/Vipers/Castror) on Beef/Blood.
experiments.description: Tested Cantharides, dried Vipers, and Russian Castror with fresh Beef and Serum of human Blood.
experiments.quote: I examined *Cantharides*, dried Vipers, and *Russian Castror*, all animal Substances, and therefore most likely to prove septic. The Flies were tried both with fresh Beef, and with the *Serum* of human Blood; the Vipers only with the former; but neither of them haflened Putrefaction.
experiments.outcome: None hastened putrefaction; Castror infusion opposed it more than standard Salt.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Chalk/Tefacea on Ox's Gall.
experiments.description: Mixed Twenty Grains of prepared Chalk with 6 Drachms of Ox's Gall, and as much Water.
experiments.quote: Twenty Grains of Crabs-eyes prepared, were mixed with 6 Drachms of Ox's Gall, and as much Water; into another Phial was put nothing but Gall and Water, in the same Quantity with the former; and both being placed in the Furnace, the Putrefaction began much sooner, where the Powder was, than in the other Phial.
experiments.outcome: Putrefaction began sooner where the Powder (Crabs-eyes/Chalk) was.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Chalk on Flesh in Furnace.
experiments.description: Infused 30 Grains of prepared Chalk with Flesh and Water in the Lamp-Furnace.
experiments.quote: I infused afterwards in the Lamp-Furnace 30 Grains of prepared Chalk, with the usual Quantity of Flesh and Water; and observed, that the Corruption not only began sooner, but went higher by this Mixture; nay, what had never happened before, that in a few Days the Flesh re-folved into a perfect Mucus.
experiments.outcome: Corruption began sooner, went higher; Flesh resolved into a perfect Mucus.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Comparison of Chalk Powder vs Salt of Wormwood on Flesh.
experiments.description: Pounded Chalk (30 Grains) compared with equal Quantity of Salt of Wormwood.
experiments.quote: The same Powder was compared with an equal Quantity of Salt of Wormwood, and Care was taken to shake both the Mixtures alike: But, after three Days warm Digeition, the Salt had neither tainted nor soften'd the Flesh, whilst the Chalk had rotted and consumed that which was joined to it.
experiments.outcome: Salt did not tarnish/soften; Chalk rotted and consumed the flesh.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.description: Tested Egg-shells in Water against Meat preservation.
experiments.quote: Egg-shells in Water resisted Putrefaction, and preserved the Meat longer firm than plain Water *.
experiments.outcome: Preserved Meat longer firm than plain Water.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.description: Infused Tectace with Barley and Water, compared with Barley and Water (without Tectace).
experiments.quote: To try whether the Tectace would also dissolve vegetable Substances, I infused them with Barley and Water, and compared this Mixture with another of Barley and Water, without the Tectace.
experiments.outcome: With Powder: Grain kept natural Size, no Mucilage. Without: Swelled, Mucilaginous.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Sea Salt on fresh Beef.
experiments.description: One Drachm of Salt preserved two Drachms of fresh Beef, in two Ounces of Water.
experiments.quote: One Drachm of Salt preserves two Drachms of fresh Beef, in two Ounces of Water, above 30 Hours, uncorrupted, in a Heat equal to that of the human Body
experiments.outcome: Salt preserved Beef above 30 Hours uncorrupted in human heat.
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.

experiments.reasoning: Observation of Sea Salt in warm Infusions on Meat.
experiments.description: Tested smaller Quantities (10-20 Grains) of Salt in warm Infusions on Meat texture.
experiments.quote: It is moreover to be remarked, that in warm Infusions with these smaller Quantities, the Salt, instead of hardening the Flesh, as it does in a dry Form, in Brine, or even in Solutions, such as our Standard, it here softens and re-laxes the Texture of the Meat, more than plain Water
experiments.outcome: Small salt quantity softens and re-laxes Texture of Meat (hastens corruption).
individuals: John Pringle M. D. F. R. S.
